decisions.reason: After several years this drain housing would likely be kept because its survival signals at least acceptable performance relative to aspirations and it remains a core component in the firm's customizable drainage architecture.

Management would likely retain this floor-level shower drainage line because it fits the firm's strategic direction toward integrated low-profile bathroom solutions and surviving since launch suggests no major aspiration shortfall.

This integrated-slope shower element would likely stay because it complements the firm's installation-oriented system offering and, absent clear evidence of underperformance, boundedly rational management has little reason to reallocate it.

The backflow-protected basement drain is a more specialized niche product, but management would likely keep it as a technically credible line unless its results now clearly fell below aspiration levels and justified shifting resources elsewhere.
